cards.text: This story starts with Elkanah, a man from Ramathaim-zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, and he has two wives: Hannah and Peninnah. Ramathaim-zophim. I tried saying that three times fast and my mustache tied itself in a knot.

cards.question: Elkanah has two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Which one has children?

cards.text: Year after year, Elkanah goes up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh. The priests there are Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas.
On the day of his sacrifice, Elkanah hands out portions to Peninnah and to all her sons and daughters.

cards.question: Elkanah loves Hannah, even though the LORD has closed her womb. So on sacrifice day, he gives Hannah a ___ portion.

cards.text: But Hannah has a rival, and this rival doesn't just roll her eyes. She provokes Hannah viciously.

cards.question: Hannah's rival taunts her because the LORD has closed Hannah's womb.
Year after year, whenever Hannah goes up to the house of the LORD, her rival taunts her. What does Hannah do?

answers.text: She weeps and will not eat
She taunts her rival right back
She asks Elkanah to send her away

cards.text: Elkanah sees her crying and asks, "Am I not better to you than ten sons?" I think he means well, but that's like me telling a baker crying over a burnt batch, "Cheer up, at least you've got ME!"
After they finish eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stands up. Meanwhile Eli the priest is sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.

cards.question: Hannah is in bitter distress at Shiloh. She prays to the LORD and weeps with many tears.

cards.text: Then she makes a vow to the LORD of Hosts. She asks Him to look on her affliction, remember her and give her a son.

cards.question: In her vow, Hannah says what she'll do if the LORD gives her a son. What is it?

answers.text: Dedicate him to the LORD for life
Name him after his father Elkanah
Throw a feast for all of Shiloh

cards.question: Hannah also vows that no razor will ever touch her son's head.

cards.text: Hannah keeps praying in her heart. Her lips are moving, but her voice can't be heard, and Eli is watching her mouth.

cards.question: Eli sees Hannah's lips moving with no sound coming out. He thinks she is ___.

cards.text: And Eli says it out loud: "How long will you be drunk? Put away your wine!" Friend, she's pouring her heart out to God, and the priest wants to check her breath.

cards.question: Eli thinks Hannah has been drinking. What does Hannah tell him she's really been doing?

answers.text: Pouring out her soul before the LORD
Waiting for her husband to come back

cards.question: Hannah explains she's been praying out of deep anguish and grief. What does Eli say to her now?

answers.text: Go in peace and may God grant your request
Come back and pray again tomorrow
Go home and wait another year

cards.question: After Eli's words, Hannah begins to eat again, and her face is no longer downcast.

cards.text: The next morning, the family gets up early, bows in worship before the LORD, and heads home to Ramah.

cards.question: In her vow, Hannah prayed for the LORD to remember her. Back home in Ramah, the LORD remembers Hannah.

cards.text: In the course of time, Hannah gives birth to a son. A SON! I'd do a backflip, but this gold base always lands first.

cards.question: Hannah names her boy Samuel. What reason does she give for the name?

answers.text: She asked the LORD for him
Eli the priest picked it out

cards.text: Then Elkanah and his whole house go up to make the annual sacrifice to the LORD and to fulfill his vow. But this time, Hannah doesn't go.

cards.question: Hannah stays home from the trip. She tells Elkanah she'll take the boy to appear before the LORD after he is ___.
Hannah plans to bring the boy before the LORD for a short visit and then bring him back home.
Hannah wants to stay home until the boy is weaned. How does Elkanah answer her?

answers.text: He tells her to do what she thinks best
He tells her the boy must go now
He asks Eli to decide for them

cards.text: So Hannah stays home and nurses her son until he's weaned. Then, though he's still young, she takes him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine.

cards.question: At Shiloh, they slaughter the bull. Then they bring the boy to ___.

cards.text: Hannah tells him, "I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the LORD." I bet Eli remembers. She's the one he told to put away her wine.

cards.question: Hannah tells Eli the LORD has granted what she asked. So what does she do with the boy now?

answers.text: She dedicates him to the LORD for life
She takes him back home to Ramah
She leaves him with Eli for a year

cards.text: So they worship the LORD right there. Year after year of tears, friend, and she kept her word.
At that time, Hannah prays again. Lean in for this one, friend.

cards.question: The last time Hannah prayed at Shiloh, she was in bitter distress. What does she say her heart does now?

cards.text: She says, "There is no one holy like the LORD." And there's no Rock like our God.

cards.question: Hannah warns people not to boast so proudly. What reason does she give?

answers.text: The LORD knows and weighs actions
Proud words will cost them land

cards.text: Then her prayer starts flipping things upside down. The bows of the mighty are broken, but the feeble are equipped with strength.

cards.question: The flips keep coming, and one sounds a lot like Hannah's own story. What happens to the barren woman?
Hannah says the LORD sends wealth, but He has nothing to do with poverty.

cards.text: He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the needy from the ash heap. Friend, I KNOW dust. I spent years under it in the back of a junk drawer, and look at me now!

cards.question: Once the LORD lifts up the poor and needy, He seats them among ___.
Hannah says a man can prevail by his own strength.
Hannah closes her prayer saying the LORD will give power to His ___.

cards.text: Here's the wild part. In those days there was no king in Israel (Judges 21:25), and Hannah is already praying about one.

cards.question: Elkanah heads home to Ramah. What is young Samuel doing?

answers.text: Ministering to the LORD before Eli
Waiting at home until he is older

cards.text: And that's where we leave him for now, a little boy serving the LORD. Keep your apron on, friend. This story is just getting started.

findings.problem: Eli first shows up here, in the line "Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas." The card doesn't say who Eli is. He isn't introduced as "Eli the priest" until card 10.

rule.text: **New people.** The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The wrong answer "voiceless" describes what is actually happening in 1:13: her voice could not be heard. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: **No near-matches.** A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: The joke line says "she's pouring her heart out to God." That gives away the answer to card 18, which asks what Hannah says she's really been doing ("Pouring out her soul before the LORD").

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "In the course of time...", "A SON!" and "I'd do a backflip...".

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: The joke "I'd do a backflip, but this gold base always lands first" doesn't click right away. It's unclear why the base landing first stops the backflip.

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the quote, "I bet Eli remembers." and "She's the one he told to put away her wine."

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: "He raises the poor...", "Friend, I KNOW dust." and "I spent years under it...".

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: "He seats them among ___" asks the baker to guess the next word of Hannah's line. Princes, priests and elders are all places of honor. Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out "princes."

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: "The LORD will give power to His ___" asks the baker to guess the next word of the line. Nothing earlier points to "king" over "priest" or "prophet," so getting it right is luck.

rule.text: **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: The card applies Judges 21:25 ("In those days there was no king in Israel") to Hannah's day. Neither Judges 21:25 nor this passage says the two are the same time.

rule.text: **Connecting passages.** When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.

findings.problem: This final story card has three sentences: "And that's where we leave him...", "Keep your apron on, friend." and "This story is just getting started."

rule.text: **Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.**

findings.problem: All four true-or-false cards in stop 1 (cards 7, 11, 14 and 20) are True. Several of them mostly restate what was just told, so a baker could learn to pick True without reading.
findings.question: Should true-or-false answers be balanced between True and False within a stop? Should a true-or-false statement be allowed to just restate the story card before it?
